Solving it forces Z_{s,t}=0 exactly when s+t ≥ min{p,q}+2, not when s+t ≥ max{p,q}. For p=3,q=2 the paper's rule would force the (1,2) and (2,1) entries to vanish, but Example exa1 (correctly) exhibits nonzero f_{12}, f_{21}; for p=5,q=2 the paper's rule wrongly permits nonzero (2,2) and (3,1) entries. Hence the asserted necessary form (gs-28) is false in general.

issues.failure_explanation: Case 2 asserts that every unimodular eigenvalue of an H-(anti-)palindromic polynomial appears as diag(λ_j I+N, λ_j I+N), i.e. with algebraic multiplicity 2n_j, and that these blocks sum to 2n. This is false: a unimodular λ satisfies λ = 1/\bar λ, so it is its own partner and can have any multiplicity. Example: n=1, P(λ)=λ^2+1 is H-palindromic (A=1, Q=0) with simple eigenvalues ±i, which Case 2 cannot accommodate (each would need a 2×2 block, total 4>2). Consequently Theorem thm-gamma-2's unimodular 2×2-block form [S_{j1},S_{j2};−εS_{j2}^H,S_{j3}] does not describe the actual parameter matrix (which is a single n_j×n_j block in Θ_{(λ_j,\barλ_j,j)} with Γ_jj^H=−εΓ_jj), and Corollary cor-1(3) claims arbitrary 2×2 Ψ_k for 'simple' unimodular eigenvalues, which is inconsistent (a simple eigenvalue has a 1×1 block; the correct parameter is a scalar ψ with \bar ψ=−εψ). Theorem thm-s-2 silently uses the single-block convention, so the paper is internally inconsistent.

Denote by $P=\mbox{diag}(U, \overline{V})$. It is easy to verify that (\ref{gs-30}) holds.

issues.failure_explanation: M is fixed at the start of the proof so that X_R=XM^{-1} is real. The proof then multiplies X by the complex unitary block matrix P^{-1} and positive diagonal D and asserts without argument that \hat X M^{-1} is still real. This is false in general: for n=1, P(λ)=λ^2+qλ+1 with unimodular nonreal roots λ,\barλ and X=[x,\bar x], one computes Φ=[0,F;−F,0] with F=−i/(2 sinθ |x|^2) purely imaginary; the SVD-based unitary factor multiplies the first column of X by a unimodular non-real scalar, so \hat X no longer has conjugate-pair columns and \hat X M^{-1} is not real. The proof also relies on Lemma lem-3 whose displayed P=diag(U,\bar V) does not give (gs-30) (one needs diag(U^H,V^T)), and on the unstated requirement that the Q_j be chosen block-diagonally so that (gs-32) holds.

failure_location.quote: It follows that $(\hat{X}, J)$ with $\hat{X}=XP^{-1}D$ is a standard pair of $P(\lambda)$, which implies that $(\tilde{X}_R, J_R)$ with $\tilde{X}_R=\hat{X}M^{-1}$ is a real standard pair of $P(\lambda)$.

Also correct P in Lemma lem-3 to diag(U^H,V^T).
